subject: sociology
title: Small Scenes, Big Meanings
welcome_lead: Zoom in on the everyday. Interactionists argue society is built one chat, gesture and label at a time.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure introducing interactionism, Mead, Goffman and labelling theory.
final_note: You can now define symbolic interactionism and the labelling process.

walkthroughs.body_html: George Herbert Mead said humans differ from animals because they use symbols — language, gestures, clothes — that carry shared meaning. The 'self' is built by interacting with others.
Erving Goffman compared life to a theatre. Front stage we perform a role (polite student, friendly cashier). Back stage we relax and drop the mask. Identity is a performance, not a fixed thing.
Howard Becker (1963) argued behaviour is not deviant in itself. It becomes deviant when powerful people label it. Schools, police and media all hand out labels that can stick for life.

mcqs.q: What is a self-fulfilling prophecy in education?
options: A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.

When teachers' expectations (often based on labels) influence pupil behaviour and achievement — pupils labelled as 'bright' tend to do better, those labelled 'thick' worse, regardless of underlying ability (Rosenthal and Jacobson).
It is a recent invention of capitalism.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when a student predicts their own grade correctly.

mcqs.q: What did Murdock claim about the nuclear family?
options: A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
It is universal and performs four essential functions in all societies.
It is a recent invention of capitalism.
It is the only valid family form and others are dysfunctional.

mcqs.q: What do feminists mean by the 'dark side' of family life?
options: The 'dark side' refers to families who live in poverty.

The reality that families can be sites of inequality, exploitation and violence — particularly affecting women and children — challenging functionalist portrayals of the family as universally beneficial.
It is a recent invention of capitalism.
The 'dark side' is a metaphor about families who don't communicate.
